title: CUDA, from first kernel to Blackwell
description: A course that takes you from your first CUDA kernel to the features of Hopper and Blackwell GPUs and the libraries that real GPU code is built on. Each track opens with an illustrated lesson that has interactive widgets you can play with (thread indexing, coalescing, bank conflicts, occupancy, the roofline, streams, FP8 and FP4 number formats), then short questions that check the idea and Python exercises that model what the hardware does, so they run in your browser with no GPU. Tracks: the programming model; how the GPU executes warps; the memory hierarchy; shared memory and tiling; parallel patterns (reductions, scans, atomics, warp shuffles); performance and profiling (roofline, Nsight, streams, CUDA Graphs); Tensor Cores and the modern architectures (TMA, thread block clusters, wgmma, Tensor Memory, FP8, NVFP4); the libraries (cuBLAS, cuDNN, CUTLASS and CuTe, Thrust and CUB, Triton, PyTorch extensions); and a capstone that optimizes a kernel step by step. Every track ends by pointing to the GPU gym, where you write the same kernels in CUDA and Triton and benchmark them on a real GPU. - [cuBLAS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/) and [cuDNN](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/): vendor libraries for GEMM and deep learning
